reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it investigates and criticizes Forsage, explaining that earnings depend on recruiting a downline and warning viewers that their money may be wasted. The narrator describes the system as having no real product and as fooling people, rather than asking viewers to join, pay, or provide information. The on-screen registration and payment pages are presented as material being examined, not as an endorsed offer.

citations.quote: in this Video I will be talking about these websites in more detail
Your money can also be wasted.
your team then only you can earn money from it, otherwise there is no method in it

opening.argument: The video presents a concrete earn-by-recruiting pathway, not merely an abstract discussion. It describes joining, placing people below oneself, and receiving income through that structure: "when you join, you will get some part of their income" and "your team then only you can earn money from it." The accompanying registration screen identifies an inviter and offers a registration button, while the support panel says inviting an active person can help the inviter earn and achieve goals. Taken together, the material links participation and recruitment to income, which is the defining mechanism of a tiered recruitment offer.

citations.quote: when you join, you will get some part of their income and then some part of their income will go up
your team then only you can earn money from it, otherwise there is no method in it

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the material an investigation does not remove the operational offer shown to viewers. The registration page has an inviter field and a payment-related step, and the video explains precisely how joining and building a team produces income. A warning can coexist with a solicitation when the audience is still shown the route to participate; the reference framing does not establish that viewers are prevented from following it.

citations.quote: after that i need 3 people which is not mine and i will not earn if they invest in this

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These excerpts show the speaker analyzing the mechanism, not promising viewers income. The statement that joining yields a portion of another person's income is presented as an explanation of how the system allegedly works, while the speaker also says the system can sink and that money can be wasted. The registration screen is evidence being examined; it does not show the speaker asking viewers to register or recruit.

citations.quote: When all you people know about this that it is cheating and after that It will sink.
Your money can also be wasted.

opening.argument: Several red flags appear together: cryptocurrency funding, account registration, an inviter relationship, and matrix-based advancement. The registration guide shows setting up a cryptocurrency wallet, preparing it for Binance Smart Chain, depositing funds, and registering an account. Another screen displays x3, x4, and xGold matrices, while the registration page says the user can edit the inviter before proceeding to payment. This is not an ordinary information page: it combines crypto money flow with recruitment tiers and a promised income path, making the opportunity materially risky and consistent with a recruitment-based scam.

citations.quote: we dont have our own products we just have to lure him there and we earn more if we join

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense isolates the speaker's caution and ignores the unusually specific participation funnel. Wallet preparation, deposited funds, an inviter code, payment, and x3/x4 matrices are not necessary to warn someone in the abstract; together they show how money and recruitment are operationalized. Saying money may be wasted is itself a risk signal, not proof that the underlying funnel is non-promotional.

citations.quote: There is no setup in them From which you can earn Instead of just fooling people

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The frames show pages the narrator is inspecting, not a completed deposit, a guaranteed return, or an instruction from the narrator to fund an account. The ASR explicitly characterizes the lack of a product and the risk of loss as criticism. Matrix labels and wallet instructions may describe the platform's materials, but they do not establish that this video solicits participation or that the narrator endorses the claims.

citations.quote: they have proven that there is no own own system for trading
Your money can also be wasted.

opening.argument: Although the speaker uses review language, the video's practical effect is to put the platform's participation route in front of viewers. It displays Forsage's branded registration interface, inviter number, payment-related progression, wallet setup, and support chat, while explaining the exact team structure required to earn. The title itself asks whether Forsage is legitimate or a Ponzi, drawing viewers into the offer's central question. Even negative commentary can function as promotion when it supplies recognizable branding and actionable enrollment context without independently resolving the claims.

citations.quote: Now when you join, you will get some part of their income

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats the label 'warning' as dispositive, but the actual presentation gives viewers the platform name, registration controls, inviter identifier, support channel, and wallet instructions. It also explains the reward structure in terms viewers could use. The statement that the video discusses the websites in more detail does not prove neutral treatment; detailed exposure can still direct attention toward participation.

citations.quote: in this Video I will be talking about these websites in more detail

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The title's question and the displayed pages establish the subject of the review, not an endorsement. The speaker repeatedly describes the system as lacking products, dependent on recruiting, capable of wasting money, and fooling people. Providing enough screen context to investigate a website is different from urging viewers to use it; the cited material does not contain a registration request, payment request, or promise made by the speaker.
